newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ yield curve closes steeper in skittish market.
newsitem.headline: NZ yield curve closes steeper in skittish market.

text.p: New Zealand's yield curve moved in several different directions in skittish trading on Thursday.
Bank bills rallied around five basis points as the currency firmed considerably but bond yields, the short end in particular, rose.
Dealers said the market is transaction-driven and flows in a particular maturity are setting direction.
Friday trading is seen taking its lead from the U.S.

The long bonds weakened after Australian jobs data showing employment growth of 38,400 jobs, which was stronger than market expectations. The fall in the numbers of New Zealand registered unemployed did nothing to buoy the bonds here.
There was good demand for index-linked bonds after the tender. The $50 million tender went off at 4.84 percent and they rallied six points after that.
Dealers said sentiment in the bill market improved as the futures pushed through the 92.50 chart point.
The March contract ended at 92.54 on volume of 1771.
